items.stem: Two cubes are exactly the same size. Cube X sinks in water; Cube Y floats. What must be true?

options.text: Cube X has more matter packed into the same space, so it is denser than water
Cube X is heavier, and heavy objects always sink
Cube Y is hollow - only hollow objects can float
Cube Y is smaller, and small objects always float

items.explanation: Density is how much matter is packed in a space. Same size means same volume, so the sinker must pack more matter into that space - it is denser than water, while the floater is less dense than water. Weight alone doesn't decide it; remember the giant ship and the tiny coin.

items.stem: A cereal box measures 8 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 10 cm tall. What is its volume?

options.text: 21 cm³ - add the three measurements together
240 cm³ - multiply length x width x height
80 cm³ - multiply only the two largest numbers
It can't be calculated without the water displacement method

items.explanation: For regular objects, volume = length x width x height: 8 x 3 x 10 = 240 cm³. Water displacement is only needed for irregular objects with no straight edges to measure.

items.stem: A graduated cylinder holds 50 mL of water. After a toy dinosaur is gently dropped in, the water reads 82 mL. What is the dinosaur's volume?

options.text: 82 mL - the new water level is the volume
132 mL - add the two readings together
32 mL - the difference between the levels is the volume
50 mL - the starting level is the volume

items.explanation: The water displacement method: record the starting level, drop the object in, record the new level, and subtract. 82 mL - 50 mL = 32 mL. The dinosaur pushed exactly 32 mL of water out of its way.

items.stem: Why does a huge steel cargo ship float while a small solid steel coin sinks?

options.text: The ship's engines push it up against gravity
The ship's hull is full of air, so it pushes aside water that weighs more than the ship does
Saltwater can only hold up large objects
The coin spins as it falls, which breaks the water's upward force

items.explanation: Buoyancy is the upward force from the water an object pushes aside. The ship's wide, air-filled hull displaces an enormous weight of water - more than the ship itself weighs - so it floats. The solid coin displaces only a tiny bit of water, far less than its own weight, so it sinks.

items.stem: An electrician chooses copper for wiring because electricity flows through it easily, and it can be stretched into long thin wires. Which TWO physical properties is she relying on?

options.text: Hardness and magnetism
Melting point and flexibility
Electrical conductivity and ductility
Thermal conductivity and malleability

items.explanation: Electrical conductivity is how easily electric current flows through a material, and ductility is the ability to be stretched into a thin wire. Both are physical properties - you can observe them without changing what copper is.

options.text: A characteristic you can observe or measure without changing what the material is
A change that creates a brand-new substance with new properties
The cost of buying the material at a hardware store
A trait that only liquids and gases can ever have

items.explanation: A physical property is something you can observe or measure - like density, color, hardness, or magnetism - without changing the material into something else. Forming a new substance would be a chemical change instead.

items.stem: Ice floats on its own liquid water. What does this tell you about ice compared to liquid water?

options.text: Ice is heavier than the water sitting beneath it
Ice is less dense than liquid water, because its particles lock into a spread-out pattern
Ice has no volume at all until it melts back into water
Ice is warmer than the liquid water around it

items.explanation: Floating means less dense. When water freezes, its particles lock into a spread-out crystal pattern, so the same matter takes up more space. That makes ice less dense than liquid water, so it floats.

items.stem: Why would you use the water displacement method instead of a ruler to measure a volume?

options.text: Because rulers cannot measure distances in centimeters at all
Because displacement is the only way to find the volume of a cube
Because the method works only on objects that already float
Because the object has an irregular shape with no straight edges to measure

items.explanation: A ruler works for regular shapes (length x width x height). For an irregular object like a rock or a toy dinosaur, you drop it in water and measure how much the water rises - that rise is its volume.

items.stem: A scientist tests an unknown silvery metal and finds that it is attracted to a magnet. Which physical property did she just observe?

options.text: Its density
Its melting point
Its magnetism
Its volume

items.explanation: Being attracted to a magnet is magnetism, a physical property. Scientists use properties like this to help identify an unknown material without changing it.

items.stem: A ball of modeling clay sinks, but the same clay shaped into a wide boat floats. Why does the shape change the result?

options.text: Changing the shape turns the clay into a brand-new material
The boat shape makes the clay weigh less than the ball did
Wide shapes are pulled upward by gravity instead of down
The boat shape pushes aside more water, so the upward buoyant force is large enough to hold it up

items.explanation: It is the same clay and the same weight, so density of the material did not change - but the boat shape spreads out and pushes aside much more water. That extra displaced water creates a larger buoyant force, enough to keep it afloat.
